title: Wire a guarded agent
intro: Build the agentic pipeline — two wires are forbidden, and both are how real systems get burned.
briefing: Route a goal to a delivered output through an agent that acts via tools and answers to a guardrail. The inspector rejects any blueprint where the agent ships output without the guardrail (unguarded autonomy) — or where the goal is wired straight to tools (tools don't pick themselves; an agent decides).

rules.label: The goal goes to an agent that owns the decisions
The agent invokes tools — actions flow through it
The run answers to a guardrail
No unguarded autonomy: the agent never ships directly
Tools don't pick themselves — an agent decides
The goal can actually become output

debrief: The chain — goal → agent → tools, with the guardrail between the agent and anything delivered — is the SDK lab drawn as wiring. The two forbidden wires are the two production burns: agent → output is autonomy without judgment (the cold-email pipeline spending money on a request the guardrail would have blocked), and goal → tools is a workflow cosplaying as an agent (nobody decided anything; the steps just fired). In the real SDK the guardrail can also sit on INPUT — tripping before the expensive path even starts — which is strictly better than judging after the money is spent.
